deepdive.sec: Metals Recycling & Circular Economy / Lead, Copper & EV Battery Recycling

bull_bear.body: 100% internally funded capex; working capital debt expected ₹700-900cr (metal-backed, hedged); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on recycling verticals over shareholder returns
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: West Asia logistics disruption (10-12% of sales); MCX aluminum hedging delay (impacting Al growth); copper import supply chain risks; integration execution risk with RML; regulatory delays in EPR compliance; commodity price volatility
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and execution-focused; emphasized disciplined capex, backward integration, and long-term CAGR targets; acknowledged near-term headwinds (West Asia, hedging) but framed them as temporary; tone bullish on copper and EV recycling as structural growth drivers
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Copper EBITDA/ton target of ₹65,000 implies >40% margin expansion from RML’s current ₹45,000 — driven by scrap sourcing synergy and value-added product mix, not just recycling; working capital debt is treated as ‘hedged metal inventory’ not traditional debt — a key accounting nuance; aluminum/plastic margins are intentionally suppressed until MCX hedging enables scale — a deliberate capital preservation strategy
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Explicit gate for new projects: minimum 25%+ ROIC, maximum three-year payback and 8+ asset turns — the deck's central discipline for screening expansion.
- Reported ROIC has stayed in a 19-31% band over FY21-FY26 (24% in FY26 pre-RMIL) against a stated 25%+ target, with drivers cited as improving industry dynamics, lower working capital and a richer value-added mix.
- Stated priorities are judicious use of capital, return-accretive growth and shareholder value creation, backed by a 15-year dividend payout history.
- Credit profile supports the reinvestment plan — AA-/AA ratings from ICRA and India Ratings, with an ICRA upgrade during the quarter attributed to prudent capital management.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Lead: 48,889 tons sold (+7% YoY), EBITDA/ton ₹23,043; Copper: RML acquired (31,200 tons capacity), EBITDA/ton ₹45,000, targeting ₹60,000-65,000 post-backward integration; Lithium-ion: 6,000 tons/year pilot commissioned (Jan’26); Aluminum: EBITDA/ton ₹16,043 (sustainable target ₹14,000-15,000), growth delayed pending MCX hedging; Plastic: EBITDA/ton ₹12,328 (sustainable ₹10,000-12,000); Rubber: 30,000 tons/year capacity planned (H1FY27), EBITDA/ton ₹7,000-8,000
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Founded in 1992 by first-generation entrepreneur Rajat Agrawal, Gravita frames itself as an integrated multi-material recycler across six verticals — lead, aluminium, plastic, rubber, copper and lithium — plus turnkey recycling solutions, with the stated vision of becoming the most valuable recycling company globally and ranking among the top five.
- Moat is described as a stack of entry barriers rather than a single edge: India import licences granted on past performance, OEM product approvals that take years, specialist technical know-how, an established multinational procurement network, and the capital/time cost of replicating capacity and customer base.
- Global credibility markers include LME brand listing for Mundra lead under 'GRAVITA M' (enabling LME warehouse deliverability), MCX empanelment, ILA-accredited plants (described as India's only), and AA/AA- external credit ratings from ICRA and India Ratings.
- Deck argues new verticals are entered off existing strengths — turnkey technology, global integrated supply chain, back-to-back hedging, deep procurement network and diversified customer base — rather than from scratch.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired a 99.44% stake in Rashtriya Metal Industries Limited (RMIL) for Rs 561.84 crore, marking entry into copper and copper alloys; RMIL was founded in 1946, runs a 31,200 MTPA facility at Sarigam (Gujarat) and reported FY26 revenue of Rs 1,040 cr with EBITDA of Rs 82 cr.
- [Acquisition rationale] RMIL is positioned to unlock high-barrier electrical and defence segments, enable cross-selling into its customer base, and provide backward integration from copper scrap to alloy.
- [Regulation] Vehicle Scrappage Policy, EPR, BWMR and GST are framed as a 'paradigm shift' driving formalisation of Indian recycling, OEM tie-ups and better domestic scrap availability.
- [Milestone] Mundra plant received LME brand listing for lead under 'GRAVITA M', enabling worldwide LME warehouse deliverability.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: Gravita significantly expanded its footprint beyond lead with the RML acquisition and copper recycling capex, driving a structural shift toward higher-margin value-added copper and EV battery recycling; despite Q4 EBITDA pressure from West Asia logistics and aluminum/plastic hedging delays, the company is on track for 20-25% volume CAGR through FY29 with 20%+ ROCE expected from integrated copper operations.
